title: PPF, PPFD, and Fixture Output
objective: Separate total fixture photon output from photon density at the crop and use each metric for the decision it actually supports.

terms.definition: Photosynthetic photon flux: total 400-700 nm photon output per second, expressed as micromoles per second.
Photosynthetic photon flux density arriving at a surface, expressed as micromoles per square metre per second.
PPF divided by electrical input power, commonly expressed as micromoles per joule.
Fraction of fixture output that reaches useful crop surfaces over the operating period.

coreScience: PPF describes total photon output from a source; PPFD describes spatial density at a receiving surface. A high-PPF fixture can still produce poor canopy PPFD if mounted too high, aimed badly, blocked, used without suitable overlap, or placed in a reflective geometry different from its test condition.

Photon efficacy is an equipment conversion metric, not crop productivity. It does not include fixture placement, room interception, spectrum-dependent response, canopy architecture, photoperiod, dimming losses, heat-removal energy, or yield quality. Wall-plug power must be measured under the actual operating state when energy calculations matter.

A fixture specification is only comparable when test method, input voltage, thermal state, spectrum, dimming level, and measurement uncertainty are known. Crop design must use a measured canopy map after installation; manufacturer PPF and distribution files are inputs to design, not proof of delivered photons.
cultivationRelevance: PPF and efficacy help screen equipment, whereas PPFD maps and DLI verify crop exposure. Keeping these roles separate prevents purchasing metrics from becoming unsupported crop targets.
A useful lighting audit follows energy from electrical input to fixture photon output, then to canopy distribution, intercepted photons, plant response, and saleable output.

measureAndRecord.requirement: Model, spectrum, rated and measured power, input voltage, age, cleaning state, and dimming setting.
PPF or ePPF band, laboratory method, test temperature, uncertainty, and date.
Fixture count, spacing, height, tilt, overlap, reflective boundaries, and obstructions.
Mean, minimum, maximum, distribution, and measurement grid for PPFD or ePPFD.
Kilowatt-hours, crop area, photoperiod, intercepted-light proxy, biomass, quality, and rejected product.

misconceptions: More PPF guarantees more crop light: Room geometry and interception determine how much output reaches useful plant surfaces.
Micromoles per joule predicts yield: It describes photon conversion at the fixture, not biological or economic conversion by the crop system.
Rated wattage equals draw: Actual electrical input can change with voltage, dimming, drivers, temperature, and measurement method.
evidenceLimits: Fixture test reports may use different laboratories, bands, tolerances, and thermal conditions. Independent installed measurements are required before comparing crop delivery or energy performance.
